:::{#exm-palindrome-machine}
#### A machine that checks for palindromes

A binary string is a *palindrome* if it reads the same backward as forward,
like $0110$ or $10101$.
A [Turing machine](#def-turing-machine) with three tapes
(input, one work tape, and [output](#def-turing-machine))
can check whether its input $x$ is a palindrome in three phases
[@arora2009computational, example 1.1]:

1. *Copy*: move the input head and the work head right together,
   writing each symbol of $x$ onto the work tape,
   until the input head reaches the blank after $x$.
   The first step also moves the output head right, off $\triangleright$.
2. *Rewind*: move the input head left until it reads $\triangleright$,
   then one cell right, onto the first symbol of $x$.
   Move the work head one cell left, onto the last symbol of the copy.
3. *Compare*: move the input head right and the work head left together.
   If the two heads ever read different symbols,
   write $0$ on the output tape and [halt](#def-turing-machine).
   If the input head reaches the blank after $x$ without a mismatch,
   write $1$ and halt.

On the input $0110$,
the compare phase reads the pairs $(0, 0)$, $(1, 1)$, $(1, 1)$, and $(0, 0)$,
finds no mismatch, and outputs $1$.
On $0111$ it reads $(0, 1)$ first and outputs $0$.
Each phase is a few states of the machine,
and each state of a phase checks which symbols the heads read
to decide whether to stay in the phase or move to the next.

:::
